ambiguities.text: No specification of rejection mechanism (silent drop vs. explicit error message)
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implicit rejection via not responding, as this is common in P2P protocols and minimizes bandwidth for invalid requests.

ambiguities.text: No definition of acceptable fallback mechanisms for obtaining pre-PoS data
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume archive nodes or dedicated historical data services must be used for pre-PoS data retrieval.
Assume standard P2P security considerations apply; potential DoS vectors from mixed-protocol networks should be considered.

implicit_assumptions.description: Block 15,537,393 represents the Paris upgrade activation (The Merge) and is the correct boundary
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect boundary could prevent access to valid PoS data or allow access to restricted pre-PoS data

implicit_assumptions.description: Clients can reliably distinguish PoS from pre-PoS block numbers
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Data serving decisions could be incorrect, leading to protocol violations

implicit_assumptions.description: Out-of-band data retrieval (archive nodes, Era files) is available for pre-PoS historical data
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Applications requiring pre-PoS data would lose access, breaking historical data analysis tools

implicit_assumptions.description: Light clients can trust post-PoS data without needing pre-PoS historical verification
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Security guarantees for light clients may be weakened
